candidates.title: Android Bench 2.0 raises the bar with multi-day coding tasks
candidates.summary: Google's updated benchmark adds long-horizon Android tasks, agentic evaluation, continuous scoring, and cost visibility because simple pass/fail no longer captures partial engineering progress.
candidates.what_changed: Android Bench 2.0 adds long-horizon tasks that can take a human engineer days or a week, including migrations, dependency upgrades, and app-building work.
candidates.why_it_matters: Agent benchmarks are starting to look more like **real project evaluation**: partial completion, regressions, visual fidelity, cost, and harness choice all matter. That is much closer to how engineering teams should evaluate coding agents internally.

candidates.title: Google and Speakeasy push SDK generation toward an open toolchain
candidates.summary: A new collaboration argues that client SDK generation should be driven from OpenAPI contracts with reproducible, inspectable tooling rather than hand-maintained wrappers.
candidates.what_changed: Google and Speakeasy make the case for treating OpenAPI descriptions as executable product infrastructure: one contract can drive consistent SDK generation across languages instead of leaving teams to maintain wrappers by hand.
candidates.why_it_matters: As agents increasingly consume APIs directly, **machine-readable contracts and reproducible client generation** become more valuable. Better SDK automation helps both human developers and tool-using agents work against the same canonical interface.
